title: Give every browser game real cover art
problem: On the homepage, every game that plays in the browser (GlobeTap, Word Duel, Perfect Circle, Don Bass Idols) shows a flat colour tile, while emulator games have full box art. GlobeTap already has a striking title image on its own game page; the homepage just doesn't use it.
why_it_matters: Cover art is what makes people click. Right now the games anyone can play instantly look like placeholders, and the ones that need a desktop app and a disc image look like the real thing.
recommendation: Use each game's own art as its card cover: the uploaded cover if there is one, otherwise a frame captured from the game or its page hero. Ask creators for a cover at upload, with a preview of how the card will look, and fall back to the colour tile only when nothing exists.
agent_prompt: In yougame.co, make game cards on the homepage, search results and the "More games" sidebar show real cover art for browser games. (1) Add an optional cover image to a game (if the schema lacks one), reusing the image already shown as the game page hero where one exists, and backfill existing games from that hero image. (2) On upload and game edit, add a cover field with a live preview of the card at its real size and aspect ratio; validate type and size the same way screenshots are validated. (3) In the card component, render the cover with object-fit: cover and a descriptive alt ("<game title> cover"); keep today's colour tile only as the fallback when no image exists. (4) Lazy-load covers below the fold. Don't change card layout or metadata otherwise.

title: Ask for a rating right after a game ends
problem: GlobeTap has 141 plays and is "Not rated yet". Ocarina of Time has one rating (2.0) and Perfect Circle one (5.0). The only way to rate is a row of empty stars on the game page, beside nine other buttons.
why_it_matters: With one rating or none, the stars on cards say nothing and a single unhappy player can sink a game. Players are most willing to rate in the moment they finish a round.
recommendation: When a round or session ends, show a small "How was it?" prompt with five stars and a skip, once per game per player. Hide the average on cards until a game has at least five ratings, and show the count beside it.
agent_prompt: On yougame.co, collect more ratings by prompting at the end of play. (1) When a game emits its end-of-round or session-end event (or the player exits after at least 2 minutes of play), show an inline, dismissible "How was it?" panel with five star buttons (each labelled for screen readers) and a "Not now" text button. (2) Show it at most once per game per player (signed-in: server-side; guests: localStorage), and never during play. (3) Saving reuses the existing rating endpoint; signed-out players are asked to sign in only after they pick stars, and the pick is kept through sign-in. (4) On cards and game pages, hide the average until a game has 5+ ratings; show "New" instead, and always show the count next to the average. Add tests for the once-per-game rule.

title: Show what you can play right now, on this device
problem: GlobeTap's page says "Plays on phones", but the homepage doesn't say which games do, and there's no way to filter by it. Emulator games, which need the desktop app on Apple silicon Mac or Windows, are shown to phone visitors exactly like everything else. And for players who did set up the desktop app and added a disc, every emulator card still says "Needs your own copy".
why_it_matters: A visitor's first question is "can I play this here, now?". Phone visitors who tap an emulator game hit a dead end, and players who finished the hard setup never see the payoff: every remix of a game they own is one click away.
recommendation: Add a "Plays here" filter that defaults to games that run on the visitor's device (browser and phone-friendly games on phones; everything on a supported desktop). Mark phone-friendly games on cards, and on an unsupported device, replace Play on emulator games with "Send to my computer" (email or copy link). When the desktop app is present and has a disc for a base game, swap "Needs your own copy" for "Ready to play" on every game built on it, and add a "Ready to play" row at the top of the homepage.
agent_prompt:
On yougame.co, make discovery device-aware. (1) Give each game a supported-devices field derived from what exists today: browser games marked "Plays on phones" -> phone + desktop; browser games without it -> desktop; emulator games -> desktop app on Apple silicon Mac or Windows. (2) Detect the visitor's device class client-side (touch + small viewport = phone; platform for Mac/Windows/Linux). (3) Add a "Plays here" option to the homepage filters, on by default on phones and off by default on desktop, persisted in the URL. (4) On cards, show a phone mark for phone-friendly games. (5) On an emulator game page viewed from an unsupported device, replace the Play button with "Send to my computer", which copies the page link or emails it to a signed-in player. Keep existing URLs working.

Then reflect the player's emulator setup: (6) Expose from the YG desktop app (via the existing app-detection channel the game page uses for "Not on this computer yet") the list of base games the player has a verified disc for; never expose file paths. Cache it client-side for the session. (7) On cards for games whose base game is in that list, replace the "Needs your own copy" badge with "Ready to play" (same position and size, a different colour family). (8) On the homepage, when at least one game is ready, add a "Ready to play" row above the feed, most recently played first. (9) Fall back to today's behaviour when the app isn't detected.

title: Measure where players drop out of emulator setup
problem: Project+ is the most-played game (13.9K plays), and getting into it takes several steps: install the desktop app, find the right Brawl disc image, add it, then play. The page says "Not on this computer yet" and "No copy stored yet", and most of its 94 comments are setup problems. The site already loads PostHog.
why_it_matters: Nobody knows which setup step loses the most players, so fixes are guesses. One funnel would show whether the problem is the app download, finding the disc, the file type, or controllers.
recommendation: Track the setup as one funnel per emulator game: page viewed, app detected, disc added (with the file type), first launch, first 5 minutes played, plus controller-bound. Show the creator and the YouGame team a simple drop-off chart.
agent_prompt: Instrument the emulator setup on yougame.co with PostHog (already loaded on the site). (1) Emit these events with properties {game_slug, base_game, platform, app_version}: setup_page_viewed, desktop_app_detected (or desktop_app_missing), desktop_app_download_clicked, disc_added {file_ext, accepted: bool, error_code}, emulator_launched, played_5_minutes, controller_bound {controller_type}. (2) Fire each at most once per session per game. (3) Create a PostHog funnel insight "Emulator setup" over these steps, broken down by platform. (4) Don't send file names, file paths or disc hashes; only the extension and whether it was accepted. Document the events in the repo's analytics docs.

title: Daily challenges with results people can share
problem: GlobeTap already has a "daily five", and Perfect Circle has a leaderboard, but both live only inside their own game pages. Nothing on the homepage gives a returning player a reason to come back today. And after a round there's nothing to share: Share and "Copy invite link" only share the game page.
why_it_matters: A daily challenge with a streak is one of the most reliable ways to build a habit, and it costs little when games already have a daily mode or a score. A result someone is proud of spreads much further than a plain link, and a "beat my score" link brings the friend straight into the same challenge.
recommendation: Add a "Today" row on the homepage: one daily challenge per participating game, with your streak and how many people played it today. Let creators opt in by exposing a daily seed and a score. After a round, offer "Share result": a small image card with the game, score and day, plus a link that opens the same challenge with "Beat <name>'s score" on top.
agent_prompt:
Add daily challenges to yougame.co. (1) Define an opt-in contract for games: a daily seed provided by YouGame (date-based, same for everyone) and a score event at the end of the daily round. Start with GlobeTap's existing daily five. (2) Store one daily result per player per game per day (guests in localStorage, merged on sign-in). (3) On the homepage, add a "Today" row above the feed showing each participating game's daily challenge with: played or not, your score, your streak in days, and how many players finished today. (4) Each tile opens the game straight into the daily mode. (5) Reset at 00:00 UTC and say so in an info tip next to the row title. Add tests for streak counting across day boundaries.

Then make results shareable: (6) Generate an Open Graph image at /r/<id> (1200x630) with the game cover, the score, the player's display name and the date; store the result with its seed. (7) After a round, show a "Share result" button using the Web Share API when available, falling back to copying the link. (8) Visiting /r/<id> opens the game with a banner "Beat <name>'s <score>" and starts the same seed. (9) Never include anything private; guests are "A player".

title: Tell followers when a game they play gets an update
problem: Games publish real release notes (GlobeTap's "What's new in v1.9" with a version history), and creators have followers (Crunch: 51). But updates only show if you open the game page, while one emulator update is pushed to everyone through the orange site-wide banner.
why_it_matters: Updates are the best reason to bring a lapsed player back, and creators have no way to reach the people who follow them. Targeted notices would also replace the banner that bothers everyone.
recommendation: Add a notifications bell: new versions of games you've played or saved, and new games from creators you follow. Mark updated games on cards with "Updated" for a week. Show emulator updates only to people who have the desktop app.
agent_prompt: Add update notifications to yougame.co. (1) When a creator publishes a new version with release notes, create a notification for players who saved the game, played it in the last 60 days, or follow the creator. (2) Add a bell to the header with an unread count and a panel listing notifications (game cover, "v1.9: <first line of notes>", time), each opening the game page scrolled to "What's new". (3) Show an "Updated" label on game cards for 7 days after a release. (4) Replace the global "A YG Dolphin update is out" banner with a notification sent only to players whose desktop app reports an older version. (5) Add an email digest preference, off by default.

title: A creator dashboard for plays, ratings and questions
problem: Creators see plays and ratings only as small numbers on their game pages. On Project+, the developer answers dozens of support comments one by one, with nothing to show which questions repeat or which are still unanswered.
why_it_matters: Creators are the supply side: if they can see what's working and spend less time on repeat questions, they ship more updates and more games.
recommendation: Give creators a dashboard per game: plays and players over time, ratings, setup drop-off (from IM-04), and an inbox of unanswered comments grouped by similar question, with a one-click "Add to known issues".
agent_prompt: Build a creator dashboard on yougame.co at /studio (visible to a game's owners only). For each of the creator's games show: (1) plays and unique players per day for the last 30 days, as a small line chart; (2) rating average and count, with the last 10 ratings; (3) if analytics events from the emulator setup exist, the setup funnel drop-off; (4) an "Unanswered" list of top-level comments with no reply from the creator, grouped by similarity (embedding or keyword clustering, cluster label = most common phrase), each group with "Reply to all" and "Add to known issues" (which creates a pinned known-issue entry shown above comments on the game page). Use existing data and auth; add tests for owner-only access.

title: Let people start an upload before they sign up
problem: Clicking Upload goes straight to "Create your account", which asks for a gamer tag and one of 26 avatars before anything about the game. The site's own pitch is "paste the HTML, drop the file, or import a link... under a minute".
why_it_matters: Asking for an account before someone has invested anything is where most would-be creators quit. Letting them see their game running first turns sign-up into the last small step.
recommendation: Open the upload page to everyone: paste HTML, drop a file or import a link, and see the game running in a private preview. Ask for an account only at "Publish", and keep the draft through sign-up.
agent_prompt: On yougame.co, let signed-out visitors start an upload. (1) Make /upload accessible without an account. (2) Support the existing three inputs (paste HTML, drop a file, import a link) into a draft stored server-side with an unguessable draft id kept in a cookie, expiring after 24 hours. (3) Show the game running in the same sandboxed frame used for published games, labelled "Private preview". (4) The Publish button asks signed-out users to sign up or sign in (Apple and Google first), then returns to the draft and publishes it. (5) Apply the same size limits, validation and rate limiting as today, plus a per-IP draft limit. Keep the existing signed-in flow unchanged.

title: Keep offensive or misleading names off leaderboards
problem: A ranked player on the Project+ leaderboard is named "REMOTE CODE EXECUTION". There's no visible way for anyone to report a leaderboard entry, and display names don't seem to be checked.
why_it_matters: Leaderboards are public and sit on the most-played page. Names like this make the site look unsafe or hacked, and other players can't flag them.
recommendation: Check display names against a blocklist (slurs, impersonation of staff, security-scare phrases) when they're set, add a "Report" item to each leaderboard row, and let moderators reset a name to a neutral default.
agent_prompt: Add name safety to yougame.co. (1) Validate display names and gamer tags on create and change against a configurable blocklist (slurs, "admin"/"YouGame staff" impersonation, and alarming phrases such as "remote code execution", "hacked", "virus"), case- and spacing-insensitive, with a clear error. (2) Add a "Report name" action to each leaderboard row's overflow menu that files a report into the existing Report content queue with the row's player id. (3) Give moderators a "Reset name" action that sets the name to "Player<4 digits>" and notifies the player. (4) Run the blocklist once over existing names and list matches for review rather than changing them automatically.

title: Count demand for Linux and Steam Deck
problem: Project+ comments repeatedly ask for Linux and Steam Deck support, and the developer answers each one. The desktop app only supports Apple silicon Macs and Windows.
why_it_matters: It's unclear how many players want it. A count would show whether a Linux build is worth it, and would stop the same question appearing in comments.
recommendation: On unsupported systems, replace the dead-end with "Not on Linux yet. Tell me when it is", which records interest (and an email if signed in). Show the creator and team the running count.
agent_prompt: On yougame.co, capture demand for unsupported desktop platforms. (1) Detect Linux and SteamOS (Steam Deck) from the user agent on emulator game pages. (2) In place of the desktop app download, show "Not on <platform> yet" with a "Tell me when it's ready" button. (3) Store one interest record per player or browser per platform (signed-in: with their account email for a one-time notification; guests: anonymous count only). (4) Show the count to admins and in the creator dashboard if it exists. (5) When the platform ships, send the one-time email and remove the records.

title: Make runtime requirements readable without colour
problem: Proposal review: RD-01's mixed grid distinguishes browser and desktop games with mint and cream card fills and a legend. Individual cards show no written runtime requirement. UX-03 already adds runtime to accessible names; the remaining gap is a visible cue for sighted people who cannot distinguish the fills or have scrolled past the legend. The image is the existing proposal, not a new design or evidence of a live failure.
why_it_matters: A player should be able to tell whether a game opens in the browser or needs the desktop app and their own copy before choosing it, without remembering a colour key.
recommendation: Validate a short, visible requirement on each mixed-grid card, such as 'Browser' or 'Desktop + your copy', while keeping RD-01's hierarchy. Accept when every card's runtime is identifiable in greyscale with the legend out of view, on touch without hovering, and through its accessible name. Treat this as a proposed refinement to review, not an adopted change to RD-01.
agent_prompt: Evaluate a visible non-colour runtime cue for mixed game grids on yougame.co. This complements UX-03's accessible names and IM-03's device-aware discovery; do not redesign the filtering or readiness model. Compare RD-01's existing treatment with a compact plain-text requirement ('Browser' or 'Desktop + your copy') derived from the same runtime data as the accessible name. Preserve the existing proposal as the baseline until a refinement is accepted. Acceptance: (1) with card colours removed and the legend outside the viewport, a sighted reader can identify the runtime and own-copy requirement for every card; (2) this information needs no hover on touch; (3) keyboard and screen-reader users receive the same requirement once in the card's accessible name; (4) long titles and requirements remain readable at narrow widths and 200% text. Record which treatment was tested and the result. These are proposed criteria, not reproduced bugs.

title: Help players recover when setup cannot continue
problem: RD-02 shows the desktop app found and 'Add your copy' as the next step. UX-06 specifies the checklist, and IM-04 measures drop-off, but neither defines recovery when detection, file validation or launch fails. This is proposed state coverage for the setup flow; no unsupported-device, file or launch failure was reproduced in this review.
why_it_matters: A checklist can strand someone after they have installed the app or selected a file unless it explains what failed and which step to retry. Restarting the entire setup wastes completed work.
recommendation: Give each blocked step a specific reason and next action: supported-device guidance, choose a supported edition, locate a missing or moved file, check the app again, or retry launch. Accept when each case has a reachable recovery path, preserves valid completed steps, and never shows 'Ready' or 'Playing' before the app confirms it. Reuse the unsupported-device routes proposed in IM-03 and IM-10.
agent_prompt: Extend the proposed UX-06/RD-02 setup checklist with recovery states, keeping its three-step structure. Define and exercise: unsupported OS; unsupported file type; wrong game edition; missing file; moved file; app-detection failure or timeout; launch failure. Reuse IM-03/IM-10's unsupported-device alternatives rather than creating another platform feature. For each state specify the visible reason, one relevant next action and the resulting state. Offer 'Choose another file' for invalid input, 'Locate file' for a missing/moved reference, 'Check again' after app-detection failure, and 'Try again' plus relevant help after launch failure. Use available app confirmations: a download click is not installation, an unanswered detection request is not proof the app is absent, and a launch request is not successful play. Acceptance: simulate every case, verify the stated recovery works, retain completed steps that remain valid, announce status changes without moving keyboard focus, and confirm the primary action always reflects the first unresolved step. Keep files local and avoid exposing file paths in feedback or analytics. This is a proposed coverage matrix, not a report of reproduced bugs.

title: Make help filters reversible and answers easy to find
problem: In the RD-02 mock, comments say support threads are already filtered out while the action still says 'Hide help questions'. Known issues show 'In progress' without a visible source or update date. UX-12 proposes tagging and an owner-editable issue list, while IM-07 adds a creator inbox; neither specifies the reader's filter/reset states or a direct route from a resolved question to its answer. These are proposal gaps, not live filter failures.
why_it_matters: Players need to know which conversations they are seeing and get excluded questions back. A resolved label is useful only when it leads to an answer, and a progress claim needs someone maintaining it.
recommendation: Use explicit All, Discussion and Help filters with the current choice visible; show a count for that view and 'Show all comments' when it is empty. Link resolved questions to the accepted answer or maintained help page. Accept when switching filters and resetting restores the expected threads, every resolved link opens its answer, and 'In progress' appears only for a maintained issue with an owner and update date.
agent_prompt: Refine the reader-facing help flow proposed in UX-12/RD-02, reusing its comment tags and IM-07's issue records if available. Use mutually exclusive All, Discussion and Help filters with visible and programmatic selected state. Show the matching count; an empty filtered view offers 'Show all comments'. Provide a direct answer/help link on resolved questions, preserving a route back to the originating thread. Source issue status from an owner-maintained record and show when it was updated; do not infer 'In progress' from a reply or copy the mock's example statuses into production. Acceptance: with a fixture containing both discussion and help threads, each filter shows only its intended set, All/reset restores all threads, and the label and count agree; keyboard and touch can switch and reset; every resolved link reaches the correct answer; an issue without a maintained status source shows no progress claim. This complements the existing support panel and creator inbox rather than replacing them.

title: Validate redesigned browse and setup on phones
problem: The checked-in RD-01 and RD-02 images are 1440px-wide desktop mocks: a long filter bar and four-column game grid, plus a two-column setup page. UX-14 checks the header at 375px and UX-09 covers headings and labels, but the proposals do not specify end-to-end mobile browse/setup acceptance. Static desktop images do not establish touch, text-resize or mobile accessibility.
why_it_matters: A phone visitor still needs to browse, understand desktop requirements and find help even when the selected game cannot run on that phone. A collapsed header alone does not prove those journeys work.
recommendation: Validate the proposed browse-to-game and setup-to-help journeys at 320, 375 and 768 CSS px, including 200% text. Accept when controls and requirements stay readable without page-wide horizontal scrolling, phone targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS px, help works by tap and keyboard, and unsupported devices get the clear alternative already proposed in IM-03. Record browser/device evidence and any gaps before calling the redesign ready.
agent_prompt: Add a concrete mobile validation pass for the existing RD-01/RD-02 proposals; do not treat their desktop mocks as proof of mobile support. Exercise browse -> filters -> game details and setup -> requirements -> help at 320, 375 and 768 CSS px, and separately at 200% text. Acceptance: (1) filter controls, long game titles, supported editions and the next setup action reflow without clipping or page-wide horizontal scrolling; (2) interactive targets at phone widths are at least 44 by 44 CSS px; (3) runtime/requirements and 'Which files work?' are available by tap and keyboard without hover; (4) focus stays visible, disclosures expose expanded state, and closing a dialog returns focus to its trigger; (5) an unsupported phone shows the IM-03 alternative and never suggests the desktop game will launch there; (6) the browser-game Play action remains reachable when the mobile keyboard is open or dismissed. Check at least iOS Safari with VoiceOver and Android Chrome with TalkBack when devices are available, recording device, browser, viewport and results. Mark unavailable checks as untested; screenshots alone do not pass interaction criteria. Keep this validation proposal separate from adoption of either redesign.
